accepted.s:
With reference to the composition of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), consider the following statements:
1. The RBI Governor is its Chairperson ex officio.
2. The Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy is an ex officio member.
3. One RBI officer is nominated by the RBI Central Board.
4. Three external members are appointed by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the composition and appointment of MPC members. The three external members are appointed by the Central Government for a four-year term.
accepted.tq: Combine the composition facts and test whether the complete list is included.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: The total strength of the Monetary Policy Committee is
o: 4 members
6 members
8 members
12 members
accepted.x: The MPC consists of six members: three from the RBI and three appointed by the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical composition rather than confusing it with larger committee structures.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the voting arrangement in the Monetary Policy Committee?
o: The RBI Governor has two votes in every meeting.
Only the external members vote on the policy repo rate.
The Central Government can overrule a majority decision of the MPC.
Each member has one vote, and the Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie.
accepted.x: Each MPC member has one vote. If the votes are equally divided, the RBI Governor exercises a casting vote.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between an ordinary vote and a casting vote.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: The external members of the Monetary Policy Committee are appointed for a term of
o: Four years and are not eligible for reappointment
Two years and are eligible for unlimited reappointment
Five years and are appointed by the RBI Central Board
Three years and are eligible for one reappointment
accepted.x: The three external members are appointed by the Central Government for four years and are not eligible for reappointment.
accepted.tq: Test the term and reappointment condition together as a paired fact.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding MPC meetings is correct?
o: The MPC must meet every month without exception.
The MPC must meet at least four times a year and normally meets bi-monthly.
The MPC meets only when the Finance Ministry requests it.
The MPC must meet at least twice a year and normally meets quarterly.
accepted.x: The statutory minimum is four meetings a year, while in practice the MPC meets bi-monthly, or six times a year.
accepted.tq: Separate the statutory minimum from the usual frequency of meetings.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: The quorum for a meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee is
o: Four external members, including the Government nominee
All six members of the Committee
Four members, including the Governor or, in his absence, the Deputy Governor
Three members, including the RBI Governor or Deputy Governor
accepted.x: The quorum is four members and must include the Governor or, in his absence, the Deputy Governor.
accepted.tq: Identify both the numerical quorum and the mandatory office-holder condition.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: The Monetary Policy Committee derives its statutory basis from
o: Section 45T of the RBI Act, following the 2008 amendment
Article 280 of the Constitution, following the Finance Commission process
Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, following the 2016 amendment
Section 42 of the Banking Regulation Act, following the 1991 reforms
accepted.x: The MPC is a statutory body created under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act through the 2016 amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the exact statutory provision and amendment year as the deciding pair.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a function of the Monetary Policy Committee?
o: It regulates mutual funds and stock exchanges.
It determines the annual allocation of Union Government expenditure.
It fixes the rupee-dollar exchange rate permanently.
It fixes the policy repo rate required to achieve the inflation target.
accepted.x: The MPC fixes the policy repo rate required to achieve the notified inflation target, and its decisions bind the RBI.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the MPC’s monetary function from fiscal and financial-market functions.
accepted.sec: MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum

accepted.s: Under Section 45ZN of the RBI Act, failure to meet the inflation target is deemed to occur when the average CPI inflation remains
o: above 4 per cent or below 2 per cent for four consecutive quarters
above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive quarters
above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive months
above 5 per cent or below 3 per cent for two consecutive quarters
accepted.x: Failure is defined as average CPI inflation remaining above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive quarters. The statutory wording refers to quarters, not months.
accepted.tq: Trap the month-versus-quarter confusion while retaining the correct inflation bands.
accepted.sec: Failure to meet the target - consecutive quarters rule

accepted.s: When the inflation target is missed in the statutory manner, the Reserve Bank of India is required to report to the Government the
o: exchange-rate level it will maintain for the next financial year
reasons for failure, remedial actions and estimated time to return to the target
names of all MPC members and their individual salaries
future Union Budget allocations and tax rates
accepted.x: The RBI must report the reasons for the failure, the remedial actions proposed and the period within which inflation is expected to return to the target.
accepted.tq: Ask what the responsible institution must do after a statutory failure.
accepted.sec: Failure to meet the target - consecutive quarters rule

accepted.s: The flexible inflation-targeting framework was first invoked for failure to meet the target in 2022 after CPI inflation remained above 6 per cent from
o: January 2022
October 2022
January 2021
July 2021
accepted.x: The failure procedure was first invoked in 2022 after CPI inflation stayed above 6 per cent beginning in January 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the starting month to distinguish the first invocation from later reporting periods.
accepted.sec: Failure to meet the target - consecutive quarters rule

accepted.s:
Arrange the following monetary-policy developments in chronological order:
A. Repo rate cut to 5.50 per cent and CRR cut by 100 basis points
B. Repo rate cut by 25 basis points to 6.0 per cent
C. Repo rate cut by 25 basis points to 5.25 per cent
D. Repo rate held at 5.25 per cent with a neutral stance in February 2026
o: B, A, C, D
A, B, C, D
B, C, A, D
C, B, A, D
accepted.x: The sequence is April 2025, June 2025, December 2025 and February 2026. Therefore, the correct order is B, A, C, D.
accepted.tq: Use the dates first and then verify the associated rate changes.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: During the period from May 2022 to February 2023, the policy repo rate was raised from
o: 4.00 per cent to 6.50 per cent
5.50 per cent to 6.50 per cent
4.00 per cent to 5.25 per cent
3.35 per cent to 5.50 per cent
accepted.x: The repo rate was increased from 4 per cent to 6.5 per cent during May 2022–February 2023, reflecting a tightening phase.
accepted.tq: Match the policy period with its exact rate range.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: The stance associated with the MPC’s rate increases from May 2022 to February 2023 was
o: Withdrawal of fiscal accommodation
Tightening
Neutral
Accommodative
accepted.x: The rate increases during this period represented a tightening stance aimed at containing inflationary pressures.
accepted.tq: Link the direction of rate movement with the corresponding policy stance.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the MPC decision of April 2025?
o: The repo rate was raised by 25 basis points to 6.5 per cent and the stance became tightening.
The repo rate was cut by 25 basis points to 6.0 per cent and the stance moved from neutral towards accommodative.
The repo rate was held at 5.25 per cent with a unanimous neutral stance.
The repo rate was cut by 100 basis points to 5.25 per cent and the stance became withdrawal of accommodation.
accepted.x: In April 2025, the MPC reduced the repo rate by 25 basis points to 6 per cent and changed the stance from neutral towards accommodative.
accepted.tq: Pair the rate action, magnitude and stance change rather than considering them separately.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding MPC decisions in 2025:
1. In June 2025, the repo rate was reduced to 5.50 per cent.
2. In June 2025, the CRR was reduced by 100 basis points.
3. In December 2025, the repo rate was reduced by 25 basis points to 5.25 per cent.
4. The stance in December 2025 was neutral.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. June 2025 saw the repo rate reach 5.50 per cent and a 100-basis-point CRR cut, while December 2025 brought the repo rate to 5.25 per cent with a neutral stance.
accepted.tq: Check each dated policy action separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: In February, June and August 2026, the MPC
o: cut the repo rate to 4 per cent and adopted an accommodative stance
held the repo rate at 6 per cent but shifted to tightening
held the repo rate at 5.25 per cent unanimously with a neutral stance
raised the repo rate to 6.5 per cent by majority vote
accepted.x: The MPC held the repo rate at 5.25 per cent in February, June and August 2026, and the decisions were unanimous with a neutral stance.
accepted.tq: Use the repeated rate and stance combination to eliminate altered figures.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: The total easing undertaken during financial year 2025-26 amounted to
o: 100 basis points
125 basis points
150 basis points
75 basis points
accepted.x: The total easing during FY26 was 125 basis points, comprising the policy-rate reductions recorded during that period.
accepted.tq: Test the aggregate figure rather than one individual policy move.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: At the August 2026 MPC meeting, the repo rate was held at 5.25 per cent unanimously and the headline inflation average so far in the year was reported as
o: 2.00 per cent
3.25 per cent
3.93 per cent
4.30 per cent
accepted.x: The August 2026 minutes recorded headline inflation averaging 3.93 per cent so far in the year. Core inflation was projected at 4.3 per cent for 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the observed headline-inflation figure from the projected core-inflation figure.
accepted.sec: MPC decision record - voting pattern and stance changes

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the primary objective of monetary policy under the flexible inflation-targeting framework?
o: Maximising Government revenue
Fixing the rupee-dollar exchange rate
Maintaining price stability while keeping growth in mind
Regulating mutual funds
accepted.x: Price stability is the primary objective, with growth kept in mind. Financial stability is also a recognised objective, whereas the other functions listed are not primary monetary-policy objectives.
accepted.tq: Find the valid objective by separating monetary functions from fiscal and regulatory functions.
accepted.sec: Objectives of monetary policy - price stability, growth, financial stability; non-objectives

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of monetary policy?
o: Financial stability
Supporting economic growth while pursuing price stability
Price stability
Maximising Government revenue
accepted.x: Maximising Government revenue is not an objective of monetary policy. Revenue mobilisation is primarily a fiscal-policy concern.
accepted.tq: Identify the non-objective by shifting from RBI functions to the Government’s fiscal function.
accepted.sec: Objectives of monetary policy - price stability, growth, financial stability; non-objectives

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Price stability — Monetary policy
Regulation of mutual funds — Monetary Policy Committee
Fixing the rupee-dollar rate — Monetary Policy Committee
Maximising Government revenue — RBI monetary policy
accepted.x: Price stability is a central objective of monetary policy. Mutual-fund regulation is associated with SEBI, while revenue mobilisation belongs to fiscal policy; monetary policy does not permanently fix the exchange rate.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-function match to reject superficially related responsibilities.
accepted.sec: Objectives of monetary policy - price stability, growth, financial stability; non-objectives

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the roles of the RBI and the Finance Ministry in the monetary-policy framework?
o: The RBI sets all tax rates, while the Finance Ministry fixes the repo rate.
The Finance Ministry frames monetary policy, while the RBI only implements fiscal policy.
The RBI frames and implements monetary policy, while the Finance Ministry handles fiscal policy and sets the inflation target in consultation with the RBI.
Both institutions independently fix the repo rate.
accepted.x: The RBI frames and implements monetary policy, and the MPC fixes the repo rate. The Finance Ministry handles fiscal policy and sets the inflation target in consultation with the RBI.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority would perform the monetary task and which would perform the fiscal task.
accepted.sec: Authority for monetary policy and price stability - RBI vs Finance Ministry

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Policy)
A. Fiscal policy
B. Monetary policy
C. Fiscal policy
D. Monetary policy

List-II (Characteristic)
1. Government, Finance Ministry and Parliament
2. RBI and MPC
3. Direct effect on demand through incomes and spending
4. Indirect effect on demand through the cost of credit

A B C D
accepted.x: Fiscal policy is associated with the Government, Finance Ministry and Parliament and directly affects demand. Monetary policy is conducted by the RBI/MPC and affects demand indirectly through the cost of credit.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure authority pairs and then match the demand effects.
accepted.sec: Monetary vs fiscal policy - complementary roles against inflation

accepted.s:
Which of the following instruments are associated primarily with monetary policy?
1. Repo rate
2. Cash Reserve Ratio
3. Statutory Liquidity Ratio
4. Open Market Operations
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Repo, CRR, SLR and OMOs are monetary-policy instruments used by the RBI. Fiscal policy instead uses spending, taxation, subsidies and borrowing.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete set of RBI liquidity and interest-rate instruments.
accepted.sec: Monetary vs fiscal policy - complementary roles against inflation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the flexibility of fiscal and monetary policy?
o: Monetary policy is generally faster and is reviewed bi-monthly, whereas fiscal measures may be slower because legislative approval can be required.
Fiscal policy is generally faster because it does not require legislative approval.
Monetary policy can be changed only once in five years, whereas fiscal policy is changed bi-monthly.
Both policies have identical implementation speed and approval requirements.
accepted.x: Fiscal policy can be slower because many measures require legislative approval. Monetary policy can be adjusted more quickly through the MPC’s bi-monthly review process.
accepted.tq: Compare the two columns by authority, approval requirement and frequency of review.
accepted.sec: Monetary vs fiscal policy - complementary roles against inflation

accepted.s: A sharp rise in food prices caused by a shortage of onions and tomatoes cannot generally be solved by a repo-rate increase alone because such inflation is mainly
o: supply-driven and may require buffer-stock releases or duty cuts
demand-driven and requires lower taxes on financial assets
caused by stock-market regulation and requires SEBI intervention
caused by excess bank reserves and requires a permanent exchange-rate peg
accepted.x: Food inflation is largely supply-driven. Fiscal steps such as releasing buffer stocks or reducing duties may therefore be needed in addition to monetary policy.
accepted.tq: Apply the supply-versus-demand distinction to a concrete inflation scenario.
accepted.sec: Monetary vs fiscal policy - complementary roles against inflation

accepted.s:
Which of the following are recognised spillover channels through which global monetary tightening may affect India?
1. Capital outflows
2. Pressure on the rupee
3. Imported inflation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Global monetary tightening can encourage capital outflows from India, put pressure on the rupee and raise imported inflation through exchange-rate and import-cost channels.
accepted.tq: Treat each transmission channel as an independent statement before choosing the combination.
accepted.sec: Global monetary tightening - spillovers to India

accepted.s: In June 2026, despite major central banks preparing to tighten monetary policy, the MPC
o: cut the repo rate to 4 per cent and adopted withdrawal of accommodation
raised the repo rate to 6.5 per cent and increased its FY27 growth forecast
held the repo rate at 5.25 per cent and cut its FY27 growth forecast
held the repo rate at 6 per cent and fixed crude oil at 75 dollars per barrel
accepted.x: In June 2026, the MPC retained the repo rate at 5.25 per cent but reduced its FY27 growth forecast despite global tightening concerns.
accepted.tq: Combine the international context with the domestic policy response.
accepted.sec: Global monetary tightening - spillovers to India

accepted.s: The RBI’s inflation forecast in June 2026 assumed a crude-oil price of approximately
o: 85 dollars per barrel
105 dollars per barrel
95 dollars per barrel
75 dollars per barrel
accepted.x: The inflation forecast assumed crude oil at 95 dollars per barrel, partly reflecting risks arising from the West Asia conflict.
accepted.tq: Test the exact commodity-price assumption used in the forecast.
accepted.sec: Global monetary tightening - spillovers to India

accepted.s: The special FCNR(B) and foreign-exchange measures introduced by the RBI after the June 2026 policy drew approximately
o: 32 billion dollars
12 billion dollars
22 billion dollars
52 billion dollars
accepted.x: The special FCNR(B) and foreign-exchange measures drew about 32 billion dollars after the June policy.
accepted.tq: Use the precise external-finance figure rather than confusing it with the crude-price assumption.
accepted.sec: Global monetary tightening - spillovers to India

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an accommodative monetary-policy stance?
o: A policy of fixing the exchange rate through fiscal expenditure
A tightening bias involving the draining of excess liquidity
Readiness to cut rates or add liquidity to support growth
A commitment to keep rates unchanged regardless of economic data
accepted.x: An accommodative stance indicates readiness to reduce rates or inject liquidity to support economic growth.
accepted.tq: Match the stance with its operational direction and policy intention.
accepted.sec: Policy stances - accommodative, neutral, withdrawal of accommodation

accepted.s: A neutral monetary-policy stance implies that the central bank
o: can move rates in either direction depending on incoming data
will always drain liquidity from the banking system
has abandoned the inflation target
will necessarily reduce rates at every meeting
accepted.x: Under a neutral stance, the central bank retains the flexibility to raise or reduce rates according to economic and inflation data.
accepted.tq: Distinguish flexibility under neutrality from a predetermined easing or tightening bias.
accepted.sec: Policy stances - accommodative, neutral, withdrawal of accommodation

accepted.s: Withdrawal of accommodation represents
o: a decision to add liquidity and reduce rates to support growth
a tightening bias aimed at draining excess liquidity
a fiscal programme of increasing subsidies
a neutral position in which rates can move either way
accepted.x: Withdrawal of accommodation denotes a tightening bias, generally involving the removal of excess liquidity from the financial system.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of liquidity management to distinguish tightening from easing.
accepted.sec: Policy stances - accommodative, neutral, withdrawal of accommodation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the recent change in the monetary-policy stance?
o: It changed from accommodative to neutral in April 2025 after a repo-rate increase.
It changed from neutral to accommodative in April 2025 after the repo rate was cut to 6 per cent, and was neutral in 2026 after the rate was held at 5.25 per cent.
It changed from tightening to withdrawal of accommodation in June 2025 after the CRR cut.
It remained accommodative throughout 2025 and 2026 despite all rate decisions.
accepted.x: The stance moved from neutral towards accommodative in April 2025 when the repo rate was cut to 6 per cent. It was neutral in February, June and August 2026 when the repo rate was held at 5.25 per cent.
accepted.tq: Track the stance change together with the relevant rate movement and later status.
accepted.sec: Policy stances - accommodative, neutral, withdrawal of accommodation
